Title: Four killed in helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Four people were killed in a helicopter crash Saturday in Rio de Janeiro, including three Colombian tourists from the same family, the country's consul told AFP.
The helicopter went down in Tijuca National Park, a mountainside forest with very dense vegetation.
Firefighters confirmed the pilot and three women "burned to death" and released images showing the smoking remains of the aircraft on a steep, hard-to-reach hillside.
Diana Paez, the Consul General of Colombia in Rio de Janeiro, told AFP the three women were part of a family group who had traveled to the Brazilian city to celebrate a girl's 15th birthday. The group of six had split up because the helicopter could only take three passengers.
The birthday girl's grandmother, aunt and cousin died in the crash, and she was supposed to take a second flight later on, with her father and his partner, Paez said.
The consulate provided support to Brazilian authorities in identifying the victims, a difficult task because of the condition of the bodies.
The aircraft went down near Vista Chinesa, a replica of a Chinese pagoda known for its high-altitude vantage point, with its views of Rio from the heart of the forest.
The monument appeared in the 2011 animated film "Rio."
In June, two helicopters collided over Rio and left six people dead, including American singer Oliver Tree and Argentine YouTuber Gaspar Prim.
Helicopter rides are a popular attraction for tourists who want to see Rio de Janeiro's famed sights and the natural splendor of the seaside metropolis.
Rio's mayor Eduardo Cavaliere posted to X that he has asked Brazil's National Civil Aviation Agency to immediately step up monitoring to ensure the safety of helicopter flights.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deputy CM: Kundasang's rapid growth was uncontrolled
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Kundasang's transformation from a quiet highland outpost into a mountain town with more than 500 businesses and a population of 20,000 had come with an environmental cost.
Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said the area, which was home to just 500 people and a handful of buildings in the 1970s, underwent rapid change after attracting farmers drawn by its temperate climate and, later, tourism.
"Development became rapid and uncontrolled. It was haphazard. That was the problem," the Kundasang assemblyman told the New Straits Times.
He said comprehensive development planning for the district began only after 2000.
He also said many landowners gradually built accommodation for visitors as tourism flourished, often without proper planning processes.
"People came because of the climate. They wanted to stay overnight, so there was demand for homestays. People simply built another structure on their land for that purpose," he said.
He estimated that about 99 per cent of homestays here do not have a certificate of occupancy.
Dr Joachim said disaster risk assessments had identified several high-risk locations, including Kampung Lembah Permai, where some residents had been advised to evacuate.
However, relocating them remains difficult because suitable land is scarce and many residents depend on vegetable farming for their livelihoods.
"This is a natural disaster area. It is on a fault line. The risk will always be there. But people continue to live there because that is where they find their livelihood.
"If you relocate them elsewhere, what will happen to their livelihood?"
The government, he added, continues to educate residents through community engagement programmes while encouraging villages to establish their own disaster preparedness teams.
Dr Joachim, who is also state works and utilities minister, said the state Public Works Department (PWD) would strengthen ongoing slope management and install geotechnical instruments and early warning systems at high-risk locations.
According to PWD records, Ranau recorded 119 slope failures along state roads, 12 along federal roads and 37 involving buildings belonging to various agencies between 2017 and this year.
Between 2023 and 2026, RM150.58 million was allocated for slope repair and stabilisation works in Ranau, with RM86.89 million spent as of July.
Meanwhile, state Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar said farmers are required to comply with good agricultural practices under the myGAP and myOrganic certification schemes to minimise soil erosion and slope failures.
He said the state had not recorded any case of farmers violating land use conditions or illegally clearing land.

Title: Heavy rain brings fear to residents
Article:
RANAU: Whenever heavy rain hits Kundasang here, Stefyanie Myla keeps her 11-year-old daughter home from school.
The 39-year-old mother of three is well aware of the risk of landslides, having lived in Kampung Kinasaraban for the past five years.
"On days like that, I choose not to send her to school for safety reasons," she said, adding that teachers at SK Don Bosco, Bundu Tuhan, shared the parents' concerns.
Stefyanie said that during severe weather, the school allowed students to arrive later until conditions improved.
"They (school) also stop all outdoor activities, and after school, they make sure the children stay safely inside the compound until their parents arrive to pick them up."
Meanwhile, Daved Simpat also worries about his two children, who previously attended SK Bundu Tuhan near here, where cracks had appeared in its wooden structure amid unstable soil conditions.
[[nid:1507080]]
"Even in my village, Kampung Himbaan, the ground movement is quite obvious. All we can do is heed the advice given and keep tabs on the situation through the village chief and the National Security Council," said the 44-year-old Gunung Kinabalu porter.
Stefyanie and Daved's concerns reflect growing fears among Kundasang residents over the increasing risk of landslides, a threat the state Mineral and Geoscience Department says could worsen.
Its geotechnical field assessments found that the proposed new site for SM Kundasang, as well as the areas where SK Mohimboyon, Tadika Kemas Mohimboyon and SK Waang are located, are medium- to high-risk landslide zones.
Its assessment of educational facilities found natural slopes containing massive granodiorite boulders just a metre away from classrooms.
Other massive boulders were found resting at the toe of slopes, only three to six metres from learning spaces.
The department's director, Dr Frederick Francis Tating, said these "practically non-existent buffer zones" mean that any landslide can endanger students and staff.
But staying home during heavy rain may not necessarily be safe either.
Tourism entrepreneur Azizul Julirin, 37, said cracks and structural changes had appeared in many of Kundasang's more than 6,000 homes.
[[nid:1507079]]
"The road from Cinta Mata to Mesilou has also shown obvious structural changes due to active ground movement," he said, adding that although residents had previously been advised to relocate, no alternative settlement had been provided.
Azizul said the district council had issued a notice in 2024 instructing tourism operators to stop accepting bookings and cancel customer reservations, but described the move as unrealistic and damaging to the local economy.
"The proposed solution was not realistic because it did not consider the readiness of tourism operators and the impact on the local economy. After that, there were no further statements from the local authorities."

Title: Kundasang's beauty under threat [WATCH]
Article:
RANAU: Kundasang's majestic view of Gunung Kinabalu, its hot springs and crisp, cool climate have made it one of Sabah's top tourist destinations. However, the growing risk of landslides threatens its appeal.
A recent study by the state Mineral and Geoscience Department found that a combination of human activities, climate change and earthquakes is taking a toll on the terrain of the "New Zealand of Sabah".
The department's director, Dr Frederick Francis Tating, said rapid development and the expansion of agriculture onto steep, unstable hillsides between 2008 and 2024 had compromised the area.
As of last year, Kundasang was home to 6,372 houses, 500 commercial buildings and vegetable farms covering 2,021.80ha, according to Ranau district office data.
"Steady deforestation and slope modification over the years have drastically reduced soil root cohesion and altered natural hydrological regimes, effectively transforming natural geomorphological processes into recurrent natural disasters," he said.
He said climate change has worsened the situation through increasingly intense rainfall, particularly during the monsoon season and La Nina weather phenomenon.
Frederick said Kundasang is vulnerable to landslides because much of the area sits on loose and porous gravel deposits, crushed rock along geological faults and clay-rich rock that weakens when saturated with water.
"During intense rainfall, these materials may absorb vast quantities of water, increasing the gravitational weight of the rock mass and destroying the inter-grain bonding," he told the New Straits Times.
[[nid:1507092]]
This increases the risk of slope failures, as seen in numerous major rain-triggered landslides recorded by the department between 2010 and 2014.
The findings were derived from its Slope Hazard and Risk Mapping project, which mapped slopes, documented past landslides, identified potential failure zones and assessed risks to lives and infrastructure.
The project employed advanced technologies, including aerial light detection and ranging and ground-based laser scanning, complemented by historical records and field surveys.
Engineering geology teams also assessed site-specific slope stability using the GeoStudio Slope/W software.
Mapping studies conducted over the past three decades identified ongoing ground subsidence and slow ground movement ranging from 0.1cm to 4.3cm, resulting in severe ground depressions and persistent slope instability.
Frederick said the risk is further compounded by active fault systems, including the Mensaban and Lobou-Lobou fault zones, where ongoing tectonic movement can accelerate slope failures.
The area's vulnerability was highlighted during the 2015 Gunung Kinabalu earthquake, which destabilised slopes and triggered destructive debris flows along the west and east Mesilou rivers.
The debris flows carried massive volumes of soil, debris and car-sized boulders at high speed, sweeping a house into a river and damaging infrastructure and bridges.
In October 2017, continuous heavy rainfall triggered a major landslide at the foothill of Gunung Kinabalu near Ulu Sungai Mesilou.
Using simulation models, such as dynamic analysis of landslides in 3D and rapid mass movement simulation, the department found that, in a worst-case scenario, debris flows in the Mesilou catchment area could reach depths of about 25m before depositing sediment near populated areas downstream.
"Consequently, our official guidelines classify the Sungai Mesilou corridor as a highly destructive hazard zone," Frederick said.
"We strongly advise against any structural construction near its banks to prevent catastrophic loss."
Field surveys revealed that some tourist accommodations in Mesilou had been built directly on the crests of unstable slopes.
In residential areas, houses are frequently built on colluvium deposits, which are loose accumulations left by ancient landslides.
He said development should be prohibited on slopes steeper than 25°, as well as in areas with extreme geotechnical instability and along the Mesilou riverbanks.
Where development is unavoidable, structures should be set back at least twice the height of adjacent natural slopes and designed using specialised geotechnical and earthquake-resistant engineering.
For existing buildings in severely compromised locations, Frederick said immediate evacuation, demolition and permanent abandonment remained the safest mitigation measures.
He urged residents to keep drainage systems clear, remove excessive vegetation from waterways, install gabion walls where appropriate and plant deep-rooted vetiver grass to stabilise slopes.
Frederick said community preparedness is key.
While the department has established an early warning system for emergency responders and residents, he said its effectiveness depends on community awareness of evacuation routes, temporary shelters and emergency procedures.
Through its Community-Based Disaster Risk Management programme, the department provides residents with geological hazard data, specialised training modules and community monitoring tools to help detect early signs of landslides.

Title: Hamas says still ready to go ahead with Gaza plan
Article:
GAZA CITY: Hamas said on Saturday it remained ready to proceed with a US-backed Gaza peace plan and urged pressure on Israel, which insists it did not agree to the latest part of the deal.
Hamas informed US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace that it stood by the latest stage of the plan, under which the militants would hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee in the war-battered territory.
"Hamas and other factions have confirmed to mediators their readiness to begin implementing the agreement and move to the second phase, provided it receives Israeli approval and that Israel begins implementing the agreement," a Hamas official told AFP on Saturday.
"Hamas is urging the US administration to exert pressure on Israel to compel it to abide by the agreement and move to the second phase," the official said on condition of anonymity.
Trump last week had hailed as a breakthrough that Hamas had agreed to disarmament under the plan, with the Board of Peace saying Israel would in tandem carry out a phased withdrawal from much of Gaza.
But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a tough reelection fight in October and wide opposition from his right-wing base to the Gaza deal, said on Tuesday that Israel had not agreed to the "draft" presented by the Board of Peace.
Netanyahu met Monday with the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, who backtracked and said Israel would withdraw only after a full disarmament by Hamas.
Israel's military also vowed to keep hitting Hamas, which carried out the deadliest attack ever against Israel on Oct 7, 2023.
On Saturday, Israeli gunfire killed a Palestinian east of Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip, said Mahmoud Bassal, a spokesman for the civil defence agency.
Some 10 people including children were also injured across the Gaza Strip, with some in critical condition, he told AFP.
But the Israeli military operations in recent days appear to have decreased in intensity, with firing and drones reported but not air strikes.
Israeli operations in Gaza have killed 1,258 Palestinians since October last year, when the two sides agreed to a ceasefire backed by Trump, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.

Title: US slams Chinese actions in South China Sea
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States on Saturday accused China of "destabilising" activity near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, saying it is using "dubious" environmental explanations to advance its territorial claims.
Scarborough Shoal is a fish-rich reef formation 240 kilometres (124 miles) from the main Philippine island of Luzon and hundreds of kilometres away from mainland China. Both Beijing and Manila claim the flashpoint coral atoll.
"The United States rejects China's ongoing attempts to enforce its destabilising 'national nature reserve' at Scarborough Reef and deny Filipino fishermen access to their traditional fishing ground," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said.
"This is yet another unilateral attempt by China to use dubious environmental and legal pretexts, backed by coercion, to advance its sweeping territorial and maritime claims in the South China Sea at the expense of its neighbours," Pigott said in a statement.
China recently published new rules on the management of the nature reserve it unilaterally created last year around the shoal, which is controlled by Beijing.
Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, including the flashpoint shoal, despite an international ruling that its assertion lacks any legal basis.
China and the Philippines regularly clash over disputed territories. The most recent incidents took place last month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tunku Azizah mourns death of first baby born through her foundation's IVF programme
Article:
KUANTAN: The first baby born under the Tunku Azizah Fertility Foundation (TAFF) initiative about 20 years ago has died.
Jaden Samuel Desen, who was born on June 19, 2006, was 20.
In a statement posted on the Kesultanan Pahang Facebook page on Saturday, Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah said Jaden held a special place in TAFF's history.
Tunku Azizah, who is also TAFF's founder and lifetime chairman, expressed her sorrow over Jaden's death and described him as her "first grandchild", having been born through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) treatment with TAFF.
"He was a symbol of hope for couples who had long awaited the joy of having a child.
"His parents, Ps. Jeremiah Vennga and Sis. Phebe Shanty, had waited 17 years before being blessed with their child through IVF treatment with TAFF.
"Jaden's birth was a meaningful moment for them and became a special milestone for TAFF, which was established to help couples facing fertility problems realise their dream of having children," the statement said.
Tunku Azizah said she was deeply saddened by Jaden's death at such a young age.
"Her Royal Highness also extended her condolences to Jaden's family and prayed that they would be granted strength, patience and fortitude in facing the loss of their loved one.
"Jaden's death is not only a great loss to his family, but is also deeply felt by the TAFF community, which regards children born through the foundation's efforts as part of the wider TAFF family."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kosovo PM egged in parliament as political crisis spirals
Article:
PRISTINA: Kosovo's parliament had to be suspended on Saturday after an opposition lawmaker pelted caretaker Prime Minister Albin Kurti with eggs, as a long-running political crisis threatens to trigger another snap election.
Europe's youngest democracy has faced three elections in less than two years, with successive parliaments collapsing under deep political divisions.
Kurti, who has been in days-long negotiations with opposition parties over a new president, attempted to delay a key vote when MP Time Kadrijaj lobbed the yolk-filled projectiles.
"Shame on you!" Kadrijaj screamed as she launched the eggs at the leader sitting in the front row of the parliament.
The chairperson of the session called for the live feed to be cut, as security rushed to protect Kurti.
But the leader appeared unshaken by the incident and said that if having eggs thrown at him was the cost of dialogue, "I am happy to pay this price."
The 51-year-old is no stranger to parliamentary disruption, with his own party members having previously set off tear gas in the chamber to protest against votes when they were in opposition.
Kurti's Vetevendosje (VV) party topped the last election in June with enough of a majority to govern, but still requires a two-thirds majority to elect a new president – leaving the former activist in talks with opposition parties.
So far neither side have agreed on a candidate, leaving Kurti in a familiar stalemate.
But after a constitutional deadline to elect parliament's speaker expired Friday, Kosovo's political scene has again been thrown into further uncertainty.
Rival MPs have threatened legal action over Kurti's request for more time to negotiate, and it remains unclear whether his request to delay the speaker's election will be allowed to proceed.
Saturday's egging, which interrupted the session before a ruling could be made, paused parliament, and another session has yet to be set.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Human Resources Ministry proposes ADTEC JTM-ITE student exchange to strengthen international TVET ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resources Ministry has proposed a student exchange programme between Kolej Teknologi Termaju Jabatan Tenaga Manusia (ADTEC JTM) and Singapore's Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
Its minister Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan said the proposal was raised during his working visit to ITE Singapore as part of the ministry's efforts to strengthen International Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ties.
He said ITE Singapore had welcomed the proposal, paving the way for both sides to finalise details of the collaboration, including student exchanges, knowledge sharing and the sharing of best practices in technical and skills training.
"I aim to see ADTEC JTM students gain broader exposure through this programme.
"That is why I raised this proposal during the visit, and ITE Singapore gave positive feedback.
"This is not just about student exchanges. It is about how we can use this collaboration to strengthen our TVET institutions, increase international exposure, and ensure that the training provided stays aligned with technological developments and industry needs," he said.
Ramanan said the collaboration could also provide ADTEC JTM students with an opportunity to understand different approaches to technical training in a new environment, while building networks and sharing experiences with students from neighbouring countries.
He added that TVET development could not operate in isolation, as it required close cooperation with industry and skills training institutions at both regional and international levels.
He said technological changes, automation, AI and the emergence of new jobs required TVET institutions to constantly adapt their training content and learning approaches to meet actual labour market needs.
"We want ADTEC JTM to keep moving forward.
"TVET must not only prepare workers for today's industry needs but also produce skilled talent ready for the future," he added.
Ramanan said his ministry would coordinate with relevant parties to finalise the programme's framework and scope ahead of its implementation.
Also part of the ITE Singapore delegation were ITE deputy chief executive officer Dr Goh Mong Song; ITE College School of Business and Services director Tan Wee Kiang; International Office, Corporate and Development Division assistant director Jenn Tan; and International Office, Corporate and Development Division senior executive Carol Lim.

Title: Camels find unlikely home in outback Australia
Article:
FAR from their origins in the Arabian desert, hundreds of thousands of camels roam outback Australia where they are used for wild races, an alternative milk source and even to make beer.
Imported by British colonists in the 19th century for transport but set free when the advent of cars rendered them redundant, estimates of the camel population in Australia range from 300,000 to up to a million.
Many of them are feral, roaming the outback and generally causing trouble – competing with stock for food, destroying fences, fouling waterholes and damaging Indigenous cultural sites, authorities say.
But domesticated they also represent a modest export market, with Australian farmers selling their milk and sometimes even the camels whole – 68 so far in 2026 heading to Malaysia and Indonesia.
Exports of camel meat totalled over US$3.9 million in 2024, according to trade data.
On the Humpalicious farm in the South Australian town of Robe, owner and former sea captain Warwick Hill sings the benefits of his fluffy dromedarian friends.
"They're very nice to work with. They're very easily domesticated," he told AFP between camel cuddles.
"If you're kind and fair with them, they generally reciprocate."
Camel milk – which he sells for Aus$20 (US$14) a litre – has a multitude of health benefits, especially for those with allergies, he maintains.
And Hill insists it's a far superior dairy compared to the "overprocessed" mainstream options.
"We haven't met anybody that can't have camel milk," he said.
"It's one of the closest milks to human milk."
[[nid:1507053]]
Business isn't huge – the farm supplements its income from the camels with tourism and a homestay.
"The market should be huge, but the price is prohibitive," Hill said, pointing to the costs of labour and the animals' relatively low milk output.
But the milk has a special quality, he says.
"Everybody would, once they tasted camel milk, prefer to drink it over anything else."
Across town, the Robe Town Brewery has found another use for the camel.
The Humpalicious farm's camels are fed grain left over from the brewing process, and their dung is then used to smoke the malt for the beer.
Sold in a dark brown bottle emblazoned with a picture of a camel dressed as the Virgin Mary, "Holy Smokes" porter is sold as a "rich, dark and very smokey" drop.
It's not for the faint hearted – a bottle comes in at 8.2 per cent alcohol volume.
"It doesn't really taste like dung," brewer Maris Biezaitis hastened to add.
"In fact, it tastes and smells a bit more like a peat-smoked malt. Smoky beer."
Further north, others are deploying the camels to more daredevilish ends.
In the remote town of Maree, roughly 600 kilometres (370 miles) north of Adelaide, the camels transform from beasts of burden to powerful racers.
Every year, hundreds of spectators descend on the small town for the annual Marree Camel Cup.
This year's Marree Camel Cup winner was Young Gun, ridden by Patrick Dennis.
Joanne Bell, 55, was racing for the first time – and took a tumble during the contest.
She told AFP she "fell in love" with camels when she was working at a petting farm.
[[nid:1507052]]
"Always wanted to be a jockey but never had the opportunity to ride horses," she said.
"So camels was the next thing and a jockey's a jockey, whether it's a camel or a horse."
"I love it because it's just something different," camel racer Kyrraley Woodhouse told AFP.
The key is to pick a camel with the right personality, she explained.
"You would want a little bit of temper, a little bit of fire in them," she said.
"Something that's got a heart, that's going to run."
Muslim cameleers – many from Afghanistan and other parts of Central and South Asia – were brought to Australia in the 1860s to harness the animals for transport in the arid interior.
Some of their descendants remain in Marree.
"It all revolved around the camels. The reason the camels were brought here was because they were so resilient," Greg Burk, whose great-grandfather came to Australia in the 1880s, told AFP.
"Camels are still dear to my heart."
Back at Humpalicious, farmer Hill said he hoped his efforts and those of others could teach people to love his humpbacked homies.
"They're quite a pleasant animal," he said.
"People come here and they see 50 well-behaved, very nice, cuddly, smoochy camels."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Father dies after jumping into pond to save son in Raub
Article:
KUANTAN: A father's desperate bid to save his young son ended in tragedy today when Mohamed Hafidz Che Din, 46, drowned in a fish pond at a resort in Sungai Ruan, Raub.
Raub district police chief Supt Mohd Shahril Abdul Rahman said police received information on the incident at about 3pm.
Preliminary investigations found the victim jumped into the pond to rescue his eight‑year‑old son, who had fallen in while trying to retrieve a plastic bread bag used as fishing bait.
"The victim's son was rescued by a worker and an Indonesian national who also assisted during the incident. However, the victim did not resurface for about 20 minutes before he was found near the stairs at the side of the pond. He was brought out, and CPR was administered several times but to no avail," he said.
Mohd Shahril said the victim was taken to Raub Hospital, where a post‑mortem confirmed the cause of death as asphyxia secondary to drowning.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Defence Ministry consistently champions better armed forces structure, career advancement
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: The Defence Ministry is consistently pushing for improvements to the organisational structure, career progression and allowances of armed forces personnel, its minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
The move aims to ensure the military's talent management system keeps pace with the modernisation of defence assets and technology.
He said detailed proposals covering the three key areas had been submitted to the government and the Public Service Department (PSD) for consideration.
Khaled said adjustments to the staffing structure were necessary because some officers met competency and performance requirements but could not advance due to limited vacancies.
"We want to ensure a reasonable match between rank, grade, level of responsibility and the strategic roles shouldered by armed forces personnel," he said at a press conference after the Pasir Gudang Barisan Nasional thanksgiving ceremony at Puncak Kasih tonight.
Khaled said his ministry had championed talent management and staffing since the launch of the Defence White Paper in 2022, while proposals for improvements to the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA) were submitted to the PSD in March last year.
He said special allowances should be considered for military personnel, given the unique nature of their profession, which requires them to attend long-term courses lasting between nine months and two years.
However, he said any criteria for expedited promotions in military service would still be based on merit and would not be automatic.
"It must be based on performance, competency, integrity and organisational needs, through established evaluation processes," he said, adding that adjustments to the organisational structure and talent management system must be implemented swiftly in line with the modernisation of defence assets.
The ministry's push follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement yesterday on the in-principle agreement to simplify and accelerate the promotion process for armed forces and police personnel, bringing it in line with other public service schemes.
Anwar said details of the new mechanism were expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, on Aug 30.
The government has also pledged to increase the ministry's allocation under the 2027 Budget to strengthen the armed forces' capabilities and safeguard the welfare of security personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 15-year-old girl drowns while swimming at Tuaran beach
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Tragedy struck at Tanjung Badak beach in Tuaran this afternoon when a 15‑year‑old girl drowned, while her friend of the same age was rescued after both were swept away while swimming.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call at 3.59pm.
In a statement, the department said the two girls had been picnicking and swimming before they were reported missing at sea. A search and rescue operation was launched using the Water Surface Searching method around the area where they were last seen.
The first victim was rescued, given initial treatment at the scene and later taken to hospital in an Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicle.
"The second victim was found at 5.08pm. However, she was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel," the statement said.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gendang 24 Perayaan set for Unesco recognition bid
Article:
IPOH: Malaysia is moving to elevate Gendang 24 Perayaan onto the world stage, with the Education Ministry set to submit an application for Unesco cultural heritage recognition.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the effort is among the ministry's key aspirations to ensure the art form is preserved, developed and introduced to younger generations.
"In May, my team and I sat down to discuss how we could assist Gendang 24 Perayaan in its application to Unesco, which is an important vision and objective," he said at the closing ceremony of the National Primary Schools Gendang 24 Finals Competition at Stadium Indera Mulia tonight.
Wong said discussions at ministry and community levels have identified steps to strengthen efforts to develop the heritage art. One initiative is the Train the Trainers programme, which equips educators to introduce and expand Gendang 24 Perayaan in schools.
The inaugural competition was organised by the ministry's Sports, Co‑curricular and Arts Division and the Malaysia Gendang 24 Perayaan Association, with Yayasan Sime Darby as the main sponsor. Sixteen top primary school teams, comprising 417 students nationwide, competed, showcasing enthusiasm for continuing Malaysia's cultural heritage.
Founded in Malaysia in 1988 by the late Tan Hooi Song and Tan Chai Puan, Gendang 24 Perayaan was recognised as Intangible National Heritage in 2009. After 38 years, it has grown from a handful of school teams to hundreds nationwide, becoming a cultural art form closely associated with Malaysia.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Mom, don't call me': Inside Thailand's deadly school shooting
Article:
BANG KRUAI: When a shot rang out at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School on the outskirts of Bangkok on Friday morning, 14-year-old Khim and her classmates peered over a balcony to see if the noise had come from a construction site.
But more loud bangs followed, until a teacher ushered them all into a classroom, checked a messaging group and confirmed to the now terrified students: there was an active shooter in their building.
"I heard multiple gunshots and felt like we weren't going to survive," Khim, who asked to be only identified by her nickname, told Reuters on Saturday, describing how her classmates moved desks to block a door, turned off the lights and huddled together near the classroom windows.
Over the next 40 minutes or so, the alleged gunman - another 14-year-old student - ran amok, killing three teachers and two school officials, before turning the gun on himself.
In all, nine people have been killed and another 23 wounded, in Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022, which has reignited debate over firearms control in Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation.
The tragedy had actually begun hours earlier, when the alleged gunman shot dead his grandparents at their home at dawn. He then took a bus to the school, 18km away, where he pulled out a gun and started shooting just before 10am (0300 GMT), police said.
GUNMAN TWO DOORS DOWN
Trapped inside their classroom in Building 5, Khim started checking messages on her tablet.
Her elder sister wrote to say she was inside a classroom in Building 4 next door, just as their mother messaged to warn about the shooter.
"I said I knew, and I told her, 'Mom, don't call me, because the ringtone might go off,'" said Khim.
On student chat groups, some photographs of the alleged shooter started circulating as he stalked through the school, which has more than 3,000 students and nearly 150 teachers, according to data from last year.
"Then, I heard a bang that was extremely loud. It felt like it was right next to my ear," said Khim, describing the absolute terror that descended on the classroom as she realised that the gunman was only a few doors down the corridor.
"I didn't know if the shooter was shooting selectively. I didn't know if he wanted to shoot the whole school."
Not long after, Khim said the teacher issued instructions to evacuate the classroom, as police secured parts of the school - but by then, the shooter had moved to Building 4, where her sibling was still hiding.
'COUNT THE SHOTS'
In the middle of her shift at a public hospital on Friday morning, 52-year-old nurse Kwan said she received a panicked call from her older daughter - Khim's sibling - to tell her of a shooting at their school.
Based on conversations on a student chat group that her elder daughter told her about, Kwan - who also asked to be identified by a nickname - said she assessed that the shooter was likely using a handgun.
Still on the phone, she asked her elder daughter to count the shots, estimating that a handgun magazine wouldn't hold more than 15 to 20 rounds: "Count the shots to see if he's out."
Police said the alleged shooter had used at least 26 bullets. Another 34 rounds were found in his possession.
"But it turned out the sound kept getting closer and closer, eventually reaching Building 4, the building my daughter was in," Kwan told Reuters on Saturday.
From another phone, she called an emergency hotline, on which the operator told her that police, including a specialised unit, had arrived at the school.
"I told them, 'Right now, I am on speakerphone with my child. He is on the second floor, clearing rooms one by one from the right side,'" Kwan said.
Without warning, the call with her daughter cut off.
Kwan said she started praying, until her daughter called her back after a few minutes. She was unharmed.
Some hours later, the family were reunited at their home in suburban Bangkok, not far from the school.
"When we are together, we fight all the time," Khim said of her elder sibling. "But seeing her this time, I've never loved her this much before." --REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israeli settler attacks drive out Palestinian Christians
Article:
Palestinian Christians call themselves "living stones" due to their communities existence  in the Holy Land for the last 2,000 years. Maybe not for much longer, believes Reverend Mitri Raheb.
"If current conditions continue, there will not be a single Palestinian Christian left by 2050," said Raheb, founder and president of Dar al-Kalima University in Bethlehem, the biblical birthplace of Jesus Christ.
Faced with growing uncertainty over economic and security conditions, hundreds of Christians have left since the war in   Gaza   began nearly three years ago, as attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians in the West Bank have become an almost daily occurrence. Meanwhile, the Israeli military has multiplied its operations and security checkpoints.
Entrepreneur Issa Qassis,   31,  is considering leaving his family and the start-up he established in  Ramallah to emigrate to the United States.
"I started seriously thinking about it about a year ago," Qassis said, adding that he feels "frustrated and hopeless" about the situation.  "Every time I move one step forward in my work, I end up taking three steps back."
Between 40,000 and 45,000 Christians are estimated to live in the West Bank, accounting for slightly more than one percent of the population. In 1967, when Israel began occupying the territory, Christians made up around six per cent.
Clergy members, officials and researchers say young Christians leave due to the deterioration of the humanitarian and economic situation in the West Bank, where jobs are increasingly scarce and movement restricted.
"Parents used to pressure their children to stay here. Now they encourage them to emigrate," Qassis said, adding that his mother, who once opposed his departure, is no longer against it.
The desire to leave the West Bank is not limited to Palestinian Christians, but there are factors making it easier for them to do so, said Palestinian Foreign Minister Varsen Aghabekian Shahin.
Christians can emigrate more easily than Muslims because they are more likely to have relatives abroad, giving them better opportunities to find work and integrate culturally and socially, said Aghabekian, an Armenian Christian herself.
The decline in the Christian population in the West Bank, including east Jerusalem, "should ring a very serious alarm bell for the Christian world", she said.
She called for "very strong action to ensure Christians remain in the land where Christ was born", adding that "the Christian world must see the reality of this occupation".
The Christian population is significantly less in the Gaza Strip, with only around 600 left in the war-ravaged territory of over two million.
Christians   have emigrated from West Bank cities in successive waves since the 18th century, with large  diasporas now established in the Americas, including more than 40,000 in Chile alone.
More than 200 Christian families have left the West Bank since the Gaza war began in 2023, according to Reverend Raheb.
Church leaders said they are seeing increasing emigration among young members of their congregations.
Christians in the West Bank are concentrated in Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, as well as Ramallah and several surrounding villages and towns.
In the town of Taybeh, east of Ramallah — the last entirely Christian town in the West Bank — churches have documented the emigration of more than 15 families since 2023. Its population, now 1,200, stood at 3,000 in the 1980s.
The town has been repeatedly targeted by Israeli settler attacks in recent years.
"The daily suffering caused by the lack of security", combined with difficult economic conditions, are pushing residents to reconsider their futures, said Father Bashar Fawadleh, parish priest of the Latin Church in Taybeh.
Although Taybeh lies just 12km  from Ramallah, it took journalists about an hour to reach it because of Israeli military checkpoints.
Excluding East Jerusalem, more than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the West Bank, home to around three million Palestinians.
A 2020 poll by the Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research found that 35 per cent of Christians in the West Bank were considering emigrating for economic reasons, educational opportunities or in search of stability and freedom.
It also noted a concern about hardline Islamic groups in Palestinian society as well as armed groups.
The centre's director, researcher Khalil Shikaki, said the desire
to emigrate in the West Bank is twice as high among Christians as among Muslims.
Now six years after that survey, he said, "almost everything has become worse".

Title: Trump's attack on birthright citizenship faces uphill battle
Article:
When the United States Supreme Court in June ruled in favour of broad citizenship rights for babies born in the US, one of the most conservative justices complained that the decision was so sweeping it would even cover so-called birth tourists.
Women "who come here solely for the purpose of giving birth" could   get automatic citizenship for their children, Samuel Alito wrote, dissenting from the 6-3 ruling that invalidated President Donald Trump's first attempt to curtail US birthright citizenship.
Undeterred by the court's ruling, Trump tried again on Thursday, signing two executive orders largely aimed at birth tourism.
That part of Trump's action, which is certain to face legal challenges, is likely doomed, legal experts said. It targets a category of people that they said the Supreme Court already addressed.
"These children are citizens based on their birth on US soil," said University of Virginia law professor Amanda ​Frost.  "Illegal conduct by their parent can have no bearing on their status."
The Republican president has for years threatened to tighten birthright citizenship as part of his  immigration agenda. On the first day of his second term, Trump issued a sweeping order that targeted immigrants in the country illegally or even temporarily on a legal basis, including those on work visas or students.
The June 30 ruling striking it down, in a case called Trump v Barbara, held that the policy violated the Constitution's 14th Amendment that confers citizenship ​to those born in the US who are "subject to the jurisdiction thereof".
To curtail birth tourism, one of Trump's new orders directs federal agencies not to recognise a child's citizenship if either parent is "engaged in fraudulent activity to obtain citizenship".
A second executive order seeks to bar visas for foreigners suspected of birth tourism, although it was unclear how it would be enforced.  Federal regulation currently bars using temporary visas for the purpose of obtaining US citizenship for a newborn.
At the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump renewed his criticism of the ruling and said "people are building businesses around" birth tourism, suggesting that "hundreds of thousands" are wrongly benefiting. Some analyses cite smaller numbers, with Penn State University scholars estimating 5,000 to 10,000 births each year from 2014 to 2024.
Besides birth tourism, Trump's new directive also seeks to expand  exceptions to automatic birthright citizenship, which include children of diplomats and hostile
foreign troops occupying US territory. The order would widen the categories to include foreign government employees and those deemed foreign terrorists.
Scholars were divided over whether courts might allow some of these expansions.
Expanding the category of diplomats is potentially legal, depending on how it is done, said Frost, "though that requires giving those people significant immunity from US law".
University of California, Berkeley law professor John Yoo, who worked as a Justice Department official during Republican George W. Bush's ​presidency, said the order's attempt to define foreign enemy forces on US soil as including terrorist organisations "will eventually pass constitutional muster".
Others said certain expansions may stretch too far.
"Japanese immigrants to the US were deemed enemy aliens during World War 2," said University of Michigan law professor Sam Erman. "Under the administration's rule, their US-born children could have been denied citizenship."
The legality of the various provisions could also depend on how agencies implement them. Some of the terms are elastic, such as the definition of an "alien enemy" or the "purpose" of a stay, said Hiroshi Motomura, an immigration law expert at the University of California, Los Angeles.
This creates "huge zones of discretion that allow officials of the US government to deny visas or admission based on suspicions or a need to vet further," Motomura said.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: NST Leader: Overqualified, underpaid
Article:
Consider this as the most dismal example of a Malaysian saddled with a mismatched job.
Distressed at his paltry salary of RM1,900 per month as a private college lecturer, he turned to cleaning toilets in Singapore and voila! He then earned RM10,000 a month practically overnight.
However, the man, whose story made rounds on social media, had to endure three-hour commutes between Johor Baru and Singapore. And that's on a good day.
If a Singapore cleaning job like his required a university degree, the batty logic would be a graduate may qualify for low-cost employment pass with lesser restrictions. But low-skilled jobs need strict work permits and higher levies.
With starting pay barely supporting an urban lifestyle, desperate graduates are diving into e-hailing jobs, delivering food, packages or driving passengers.
Up to May, Malaysia's unemployment rate was three per cent, representing 513,400 jobless Malaysians.
However, jobs are there for practically everyone, just not the ones they are qualified for because skills mismatch and underemployment are problematic.
Thirty-six per cent of highly educated workers are competing for semi-skilled or low-skilled jobs, a percentage reaffirmed by Armed Forces Fund Board chief executive Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi.
The mismatch, Ashraf lamented, reflected a key structural challenge in Malaysia's labour market and yet, the strategic sectors of energy, digital and manufacturing are always facing a shortage of skilled workers.
Juxtaposing the easy-to-get jobs with mismatched ones has produced this paradox: job losses and applications have risen to create stable unemployment, but it operates within pressures of corporate retrenchments.
Why? Malaysia creates plentiful low-tier retail and administrative jobs but can't generate enough high-paying and high-value tech or corporate jobs.
The employers' penchant for perennial staff replacements forces stagnation of wages that fail to measure up with inflation.
This is compounded by Malaysia's dense reliance on low-to-medium-skilled workers in plantations, construction and services.
Then there's the university system's old dogma: producing graduates struggling to keep up with digital transformation, artificial intelligence and specialised technical and vocational education and training.
Obviously, we need a quick course-correction: shift from low-cost, assembly-based economy to a high-value, tech-driven hub.
However, it demands well-thought government interventions in economic policy, wage restructuring and high education adjustments.
This won't be popular: employers must devise a mechanism to adjust pay scales of RM1,800 to RM2,500 to neutralise entry-level salary compression.
This needs re-energising: the old saw of profits and productivity gains shared equitably with employees simultaneously with government offensive for progressive wages.
Breaking the dependence on foreign workers is hard because the high cost of industrialisation and automation.
But if this continues, this is inevitable: huge talent flees abroad, much to Malaysia's detriment. That Singapore toilet-cleaning gig, a sacrilege here, is looking more attractive by the day.

Title: Thailand school shooting toll rises to nine after death of 12-year-old girl, police say
Article:
BANGKOK: The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine today after police said a 12-year-old girl who was caught in Friday's incident had died.
Police at Plai Bang Police Station in Nonthaburi province told Reuters that the girl died today, a day after a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot his grandparents before killing five people at his school and turning the gun on himself.
The suspect, who was also a student, allegedly
shot his grandparents
before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, killing five teachers and staff members on Friday.
Twenty-one others were injured, eight of them critically. The suspect was later found dead at the school.
Hours after the shooting, Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul vowed to introduce a
new firearms control law
in Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation.
Anutin, who previously tightened gun laws when he was interior minister, said he would propose legislation to restrict the carrying of firearms by members of the public.
"The new law will only allow government officials on duty to carry guns," he told reporters on Friday, but did not provide details of the proposed legislation, including whether it would tighten gun ownership requirements.

Title: Three men arrested over viral hotel brawl in Johor Baru
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested three men believed to be involved in a fight at a hotel here on Thursday, which was captured in a video that went viral on social media.
Johor Baru South district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police received information about the incident about 12.55pm today.
"Preliminary investigations indicate that the fight took place about 4pm on Thursday and was believed to have been triggered by dissatisfaction among those involved, with several people also believed to have been under the influence of alcohol.
"Following the information received, police arrested the three men, aged between 35 and 56, in front of the hotel about 3pm today," he said in a statement.
Azrul Hisham said checks showed that the trio had a combined total of 25 previous records involving criminal and drug-related offences.
He added that initial urine screening tests found all three suspects negative for drugs.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting while armed and Regulation 25(1)(n) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 for failing to produce identification cards.
"Police will apply for a remand order against the three suspects at the magistrate's court here tomorrow.
"Efforts are also ongoing to trace other suspects believed to have been involved in the incident," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six remanded seven days over kidnapping of two foreigners in Alor Star
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six people arrested to assist in investigations into the kidnapping of two foreigners in Alor Star have been remanded for seven days from today.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects comprised a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, who were arrested in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur.
"All six have been remanded until Aug 14 to facilitate investigations," he said when contacted today.
Yesterday
, two foreigners
were shot dead in an exchange of fire with police during an operation to rescue the two kidnapping victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata, in Alor Star, about 8.40pm.
The operation also resulted in the rescue of the two victims, a foreign man in his 70s and a foreign woman in her 30s, who were found blindfolded and handcuffed.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, which covers kidnapping for ransom.

Title: Penang puts ANPR parking enforcement on hold amid public concerns
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has instructed both local authorities in the state to immediately suspend the implementation of the Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for issuing compounds, pending a review.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was made after the state government took into account public feedback and views on the system's implementation.
"The state government will instruct both local authorities, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), to immediately suspend the implementation of ANPR and review its details.
"What is important is that we listen to the people's voices, review what needs to be reviewed, and ensure that every policy implemented truly takes into account the interests of the people of Penang," he said in a Facebook post tonight.
Chow said the matter was among those discussed during a meeting with Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim and Penang DAP deputy chairman Zairil Khir Johari after he chaired the Penang Pakatan Harapan Leadership Council meeting here today.
He said they also discussed several issues concerning the livelihood of Penang residents, particularly the economic challenges currently being faced, with several related measures to be detailed and announced in the near future.
Yesterday, MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the use of the ANPR system by MBPP, which began on April 24 last year, had resulted in an average of about 7,000 parking offence compounds being issued each month.
He said the number of compounds showed that the technology had helped improve the efficiency of parking enforcement, particularly as the number of parking bays managed by the local authority on the island had reached nearly 20,000.
The ANPR system, which began operating on April 24, 2025, involving two vehicles, enabled MBPP to detect parking offences more accurately than manual inspection methods.
However, its implementation had caused unease and concern among Penang residents, including former chief minister Lim Guan Eng.

Title: Kelantan police arrest 14,460 in anti drug crackdown
Article:
KOTA BARU: A total of 14,460 drug pushers and addicts were arrested in Kelantan during anti-drug operations in the first six months of this year.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the arrests, involving 13,950 drug cases, were recorded between January and June.
He said the operations were aimed at dismantling drug syndicates, particularly in border districts such as Pasir Mas and Tumpat.
Mohd Yusoff said police had also introduced a strategy requiring every district police station chief to make at least one drug-related arrest daily. The measure took effect on July 15.
"At the district police station level, officers are required to arrest at least one drug trafficker or dealer every week.
"At the state contingent level, our focus is on major drug traffickers and syndicates," he said.
Mohd Yusoff said the strategy comprised four main thrusts: dismantling drug syndicates, increasing charges and convictions through thorough investigations, blocking drugs from entering Kelantan through border and smuggling routes, and strengthening prevention efforts.
"Never be tempted by offers of huge sums of money because once you become involved, you could lose your freedom, bring shame to your family and destroy your future.
"Do not allow your lifestyle and future to be ruined by the drug trade," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says Malaysia will not be transit route for Israel-bound trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed appreciation to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) for its swift action in seizing a container suspected of carrying strategic goods for export to Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor yesterday.
In a Facebook post today, he said the action demonstrated Malaysia's firmness in ensuring the country did not become a transit route for trade that could support or contribute to the Israeli regime's atrocities against the Palestinian people.
"It is also in line with Malaysia's commitment under The Hague Group, as well as the ban that has been in effect since December 2023 prohibiting Israeli ships and vessels carrying cargo to Israel from using the country's ports," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia would continue to uphold the principles of humanity, justice and international law in defending the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people.
Earlier, MCBA said it had detained and inspected a container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas yesterday that was suspected of carrying goods for export to Israel.
The agency said the shipment was suspected of violating Item No. 15 of the Second Schedule of the Customs (Prohibition of Exports) Order 2023, which prohibits the direct or indirect export of goods to Israel in accordance with the Malaysian government's policies and directives. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Highway fight: Police track Perodua driver after viral Ferrari road rage assault [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down the driver of a Perodua Aruz who allegedly assaulted a Ferrari driver during a fight on the North-South Expressway (Plus) that went viral on social media today.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said police received a report from one of the drivers involved at 6.40pm today.
He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred around 11am at KM276 of the Plus highway heading towards Seremban.
"The incident is believed to have stemmed from a driving dispute between two men in their 30s.
"The suspect allegedly assaulted the victim, causing him to fall, and made criminal threats against him.
"The incident was later broken up by members of the public," he said in a statement today.
Johari said police had identified the suspect and the vehicle involved and were working to locate him.
The case is being investigated under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code.
He urged anyone with information to contact the Nilai district police headquarters operations room or any nearby police station.
Johari also advised the public against speculation that could interfere with the investigation.
Earlier, a video circulating on social media showed a Ferrari and a Perodua Aruz stopped in the right-most lane of the highway.
The footage also showed two men, believed to be the drivers, wrestling and fighting before one of them fell to the ground.
Members of the public subsequently intervened to break up the fight.

Title: UAE accuses Iran of targeting ADNOC tanker in Hormuz
Article:
DUBAI: The United Arab Emirates on Saturday said Iran had targeted a tanker belonging to the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait and wants to charge users for passage, which the US fiercely opposes, and is in talks with nearby Oman over arrangements for the strait's future management.
The UAE foreign ministry in a statement condemned what it called a "hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties."
On Friday, ADNOC had put out a statement saying that since the start of the war, 15 of its vessels had been attacked in Hormuz, "including three vessels this week alone."
Before US-Israeli strikes in February kicked off what quickly became a regional war, Hormuz carried around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday said that talks with Oman were "approaching the final stages" but cautioned that "this is not a sign of the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz."
"The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation of the memorandum of understanding by the United States," he said, referencing a June agreement between the US and Iran to set terms for peace talks.
The Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the Iranian military, underscored the point on Saturday, saying: "The opening of the Strait of Hormuz has its own mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman."
"The enemy is forced to accept Iran's conditions for the opening of the strait and to refrain from the interference that it is currently making in the negotiations – which have almost reached their end – between Iran, Oman and other countries."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCKK can re-emerge with revitalised role in modern era, says Sultan Nazrin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heritage schools such as the Malay College Kuala Kangsar (MCKK) can re-emerge and take on a revitalised role in the modern era by adapting to the profoundly different context in which they now operate, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said today.
His Royal Highness said a new approach was needed, one that suited current times while building on the strong ethical and educational foundations that had long defined such schools.
Sultan Nazrin, who is Royal Patron of the MCKK Board of Governors, said MCKK and similar schools must adapt and transform in response to new realities, particularly a future shaped by increasingly capable artificial intelligence (AI) and rapid technological change.
The Ruler said the education system must be reimagined and re-equipped to better prepare future generations for an era shaped by AI, enabling it to deliver more effectively what would be needed in the years ahead.
"(This is) so that the next generation may be better able to reap the benefits of the AI age we are entering," Sultan Nazrin said when launching the book Breaking, But Not Broken, which offers a candid assessment of the challenges currently faced by the prestigious boarding school here today.
Sultan Nazrin said the goal was not only to develop human capital that could adapt to evolving economic dynamics driven by rapid technological change but also to cultivate well-rounded human beings, young people whose skills, sensitivities and values are all essential to their contribution and role in society.
"Both elements, the practical and the more intangible, are always important. But in this current period of dramatic and unpredictable transformation, it becomes even more vital that our education system can deliver both these qualities," the Ruler said.
On the book, Sultan Nazrin commended the authors - Ghazally Ismail, Ahmad Ibrahim and Hisham Badrul Hashim - for their courage in addressing the sensitive subject.
The Ruler said the authors' analysis of the challenges MCKK faces is unflinching, even harsh, at times.
Sultan Nazrin said their assessment extends to the select few older residential schools, equally celebrated, and equally, it seems, in decline.
"These institutions, designated as 'power' schools, have seen their powers sadly dimmed, and their long-standing ability to produce graduates of the very highest calibre is no longer as assured as it once was.
"Command of language, critical thinking, even a commitment to serve - all are deemed lacking in today's graduates. And this, of course, is in marked contrast to the past," His Royal Highness added.
Meanwhile, MCKK Board of Governors chairman Tan Sri Dr Ahmad Tajuddin Ali said the MCKK Foundation has received more than RM36 million in donations and contributions since its establishment in 2008.
He said more than RM19 million of the funds had been invested in new infrastructure, including the IB Complex and Auditorium Tun Abdul Razak, adding that another RM3.5 million had been spent on refurbishment and restoration works, including improvements to the Pavilion Hostel, Prep School toilets, gymnasium roof, swimming pool and other essential facilities.
"Beyond physical infrastructure, the Foundation has also built a strong and sustainable endowment.
"Today, the Foundation manages endowment funds exceeding RM16 million, contributed by generous benefactors including Petronas and His Majesty Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei Darussalam.
"To date, more than RM7 million in investment income has been channelled back to the College," he said during his speech.
Ahmad Tajuddin said the investment income had supported scholarships and financial assistance for deserving students, leadership development programmes, participation in international conferences and competitions, teacher professional development, campus maintenance and the preservation of the College's heritage buildings and grounds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: I was in Sabah when PKR discussed Nurul Izzah's resignation
Article:
SANDAKAN: Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he was not present at the party meeting that discussed Nurul Izzah Anwar's decision to resign as PKR deputy president.
Saifuddin, who was recently appointed as a
PKR vice-president
, said he was in Sabah on official duties when the meeting was held yesterday.
"I was not at the meeting because I was in Sabah at the time.
"The meeting was held yesterday and I was carrying out official duties in Sabah," he said at a press conference after an Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) familiarisation programme with 14 diplomatic and foreign representatives here today.
He was asked to comment on yesterday's PKR Central Leadership Council meeting, which decided to
place Nurul Izzah on temporary leave
beginning after the 2026 National Congress.
The council also appointed Saifuddin Nasution to temporarily assume the duties of deputy president.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil was reported to have said the decision was made after the council considered Nurul Izzah's request to step down from the position, as well as hearing her views and those of the party leadership.
Nurul Izzah was reported to have said in a statement yesterday that she made the decision to relinquish the post after careful consideration to enable her to pursue further studies.
